title: Separate startup phases and minimal runtime linking for GPU deps to reduce cold-start jitter
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Cold-start and instance-restart jitter from eager linking and full dependency probing (CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS stacks) causes latency spikes and noisy telemetry for short-lived worker tasks. Goal: decouple instance bootstrap into deterministic phases and move non-critical dependency resolution off the hot path via a minimal runtime-linking model and on-demand kernel imports. This reduces tail latency and makes runtime failures easier to isolate and rollback.
motivation_and_background: Several recent incidents and internal benchmarks show ~70ms median startup but 350-800ms p99 spikes on mixed GPU fleets where the runtime eagerly walks the dependency graph and resolves multiple shared objects. Our existing approaches (full prelink, heavy probe) are brittle across kernel ABI variants and make safe rollbacks harder. This ticket experiments with a tiered startup: 1) essential init (memory, RPC, basic kernel dispatch stubs), 2) deferred probe (load non-critical kernels and quantized paths on first use), 3) background validation (validate optional kernels and telemetry-only probes).
outcome_metrics: reduce p99 cold-start latency by >= 40% on mixed fleets
reduce variance (stddev) of startup times by >= 30%
no increase in runtime dispatch failure rate (<= 0.1% for 30d)
approach_summary: Implement a minimal ELF-symbol binding stage that resolves only dispatcher entrypoints and a small set of ABI-stable helpers at bootstrap. Provide a background worker that performs best-effort resolution for optional kernels and prefetches kernel code for high-frequency model families. Add feature gates to opt into eager vs deferred linking per deployment class (hosted vs dedicated). Include robust telemetry to detect failed lazy loads and a fast soft-fallback to a safe, widely-compatible kernel variant.

Runtime: implement 'core_bind' path that only binds 12 symbols (owner: backend team)

acceptance_criteria: All unit and integration tests pass in CI with new lazy-binding enabled
Canary rollout shows >= 40% p99 improvement without increase in kernel-load errors
Feature gate available in console and default policy for hosted is conservative (deferred for mixed fleets)
Runbook and rollback steps published in Engineering Confluence and linked in PR description
No silent crashes: any lazy-load failure triggers clear error metric and falls back to compatible model variant within 500ms
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: lazy bind fails in production because symbol names differ in an older CUTLASS build; Mitigation: maintain a short whitelist of ABI-safe symbols and keep a compatibility shim to translate mismatches
Risk: background loader increases memory pressure; Mitigation: rate-limit background work and implement LRU for kernel prefetch cache
Risk: rollout causes user-facing regressions for VIP customers; Mitigation: add per-customer opt-out and start with dedicated fleet canaries
testing_and_validation: Add synthetic cold-start harness that creates short-lived worker processes across hetero nodes
Run mixed-model throughput traces from production traces to validate warmup behavior
Chaos: simulate missing shared object at runtime and ensure fallback kicks in and is observable
Benchmarks: compare baseline and new startup over 5M requests with p50/p95/p99 breakdowns
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag and enable on internal infra cluster
Run 24h soak and smoke tests; validate no increase in error rate
Enable 10% production canary for low-traffic regions with observability dashboard
If stable, expand to 50% and run 72h A/B comparisons; if metrics hold, full rollout
Provide immediate rollback toggle in console if kernel-load error rate > 0.5% for 15m
